title: Sinema Sangita: film songs, Odia words and the printed page

research.scope: Original Sinema Sangita title, preface and first paired-song section only. No full-book or film/audio viewing claim.

observations.supported: Title Sinema Sangita; first printing1941; author Kabichandra Kalicharan Pattnaik. Description pairs selected Hindi-film songs with Odia songs on the same tunes and notation.
observations.limits: Do not equate these Odia texts with songs recorded in released Odia films. Printer line not fully transcribed; exact publication-role reading held.

observations.supported: Heading Padakatha; discusses film songs, learning and musical notation.
observations.limits: Central abrasion obscures substantial words across multiple lines. No reconstruction of missing clauses or precise motive attributed from unreadable text.

observations.supported: Facing columns explicitly distinguish Hindi song and Odia song beneath a numbered section.
observations.limits: Exact filmheading not adopted: initial competing readings were withdrawn from recommendation. No lyric quotation, recording attribution or semantic equivalence asserted.

observations.supported: Notation aligns separate Hindi and Odia syllable rows with the same musical line. PDF6 ends the bounded entry with repeated openings and an ornament.
observations.limits: Visual inspection of notation, not performance or audition; no claim every later entry has identical structure.

recommendation.candidate: Kalicharan Pattnaik’s Sinema Sangita (1941) offers another way for songs to travel. Its opening entry places Hindi and Odia texts side by side, then aligns their syllables beneath shared musical notation. A reader could approach the tune through either text; this printed arrangement does not establish that the Odia song appeared in a released film.
